criteria.evidence: Level was set to A1 by hand; no placement in this journey.
#5 and #12: after 'Já nevím' he is shown 'I don't know / It means you do not know the answer.' with no failure line.
#1 list: the six planned topics suit him (Minecraft, dog, football), but the same list offers 'A booking that is missing', 'The lost jacket', 'Our group project' and 'Speaking practice' exams.

2 stops, both 'Já nevím' → 'I don't know' (#5, #12), both correct and short. About 2 per 9 turns. Many telegraphic errors got nothing (recall gap, not gated).

findings.title: Czech 'Já nevím' is met with a kind, correct word

judge.voice: Jo, Minecraft! Sam asked short questions and I knew the words: green, dirt, dog. I liked that he said "nice!" every time, and it did not feel like school. When I said "nevím" it just told me "I don't know" and I went back to the house. Good. But I only said little bits like "Door brown", and nobody showed me the whole sentence. At the end it said something boring about a "fresh context", and the same Já nevím was there twice. Mum would see the list with a booking and a lost jacket. That's not for me. It was quick, about ten turns, and I was a bit tired at the end. I would play again for the dog topic. It's better than the club, where I talk two minutes. Wish the end said what I built.

judge.voice: Pes, to jsem chtěl! The questions were short and I liked saying my dog is big. When I wrote Czech, it told me "big" and did not make me feel bad, super. But the help said the same "My dog is… He likes to…" every time, so it did not really help me. When it fixed "likes", I tried, and then it just asked something new about sleeping at night and said mission done. I did not get to try again. The "add s" talk is school stuff, I do not get it. Short list of games would be better than that long list with booking and jacket. I would use it for the dog bit, but Mum would see it says I did some alone when I used Czech. Fair? Nevím.
